25:6.headline: Rashi reads the short spelling of "concubines" as one woman, Hagar
25:6.body: The plural הפילגשים is spelled short, which Rashi takes to mean only one concubine, Hagar, who is also Keturah. Rashbam instead names two women, Hagar and Keturah.

sources.quote: חָסֵר כְּתִיב, שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה אֶלָּא פִּלֶגֶשׁ אַחַת, הִיא הָגָר, הִיא קְטוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word is written short, so there was only one concubine, Hagar, who is Keturah.

sources.quote: הפילגשים - הגר וקטורה
sources.says: Rashbam says the concubines were Hagar and Keturah.

25:8.headline: The word for Abraham's death is one Rashi saves for the righteous
25:8.body: Ibn Ezra says ויגוע means the spirit leaves the body in one moment, with no long suffering. Rashi, on the same word for Ishmael in verse 17, says it is said only of the righteous.

sources.quote: צאת הרוח מהגוף רגע אחד בלי עינוי ועיכוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means the spirit leaves the body in a single moment, with no suffering or delay.

sources.quote: לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה גְוִיעָה אֶלָּא בְּצַדִּיקִים
sources.says: Rashi, on Ishmael's death in verse 17, says this word is used only of the righteous.

25:8.headline: Abraham was "full" of what? Commentators give two answers
25:8.body: The verse says שבע, "satisfied", but not with what. Ramban says Abraham saw all his heart's wishes come true, while Kli Yakar says it means full of days, even though the verse does not say "days".

sources.quote: שֶׁרָאָה כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ וְשָׂבַע כָּל טוֹבָה
sources.says: Ramban says Abraham saw all his heart's wishes and was satisfied with every good thing.

sources.quote: שֶׁגַּם בְּאַבְרָהָם קָאֵי ״וְשָׂבֵעַ״ עַל הַיָּמִים
sources.says: Kli Yakar says that for Abraham too, "satisfied" refers to days.

25:21.headline: Isaac's prayer uses a word that means pressing again and again
25:21.body: Rashi says the word means he prayed a great deal and pressed hard. Rashbam says it means piling up words, and points to another verse where the same word is used that way.

sources.quote: הִרְבָּה וְהִפְצִיר בִּתְפִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says Isaac prayed at length and pressed hard.

sources.quote: ויעתר - רבוי דברים, כדכתיב: העתרתם עלי דבריכם
sources.says: Rashbam says the word means a multiplying of words, and compares "you have multiplied your words against me".

25:22.headline: The twins "struggle" in the womb, but the word may mean "run"
25:22.body: Rashi says the sages read ויתרוצצו as ריצה, running: Jacob ran to get out when his mother passed a house of Torah, and Esau when she passed idol worship. Rashbam also takes the word from running, not from crushing.

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ לְשׁוֹן רִיצָה; כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה עוֹבֶרֶת עַל פִּתְחֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁל שֵׁם וָעֵבֶר יַעֲקֹב רָץ וּמְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת, עוֹבֶרֶת עַל פֶּתַח עֲבוֹדַת אֱלִילִים, עֵשָׂו מְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as running: Jacob ran to leave at a house of Torah, and Esau at an idol house.

sources.quote: לשון רץ לקראת רץ, שהיו רצים ומתנענעים בתוך גופה כדרך עוברים
sources.says: Rashbam says it means one running toward another, as babies move about inside the mother.

25:23.headline: The written spelling of "nations" points to Rabbi and Antoninus
25:23.body: The verse is written גיים but read גוֹיִם, "nations". Radak says the sages read the written form like גאים, "proud ones", and apply it to Rabbi and Antoninus.

sources.quote: גיים כְּתִיב; אֵלּוּ אַנְטוֹנִינוּס וְרַבִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it is written גיים and refers to Antoninus and Rabbi.

sources.quote: וְדָרְשׁוּ (עבודה זרה יא) הַכְּתָב כְּמוֹ גֵּאִים, זֶהוּ רַבִּי וְאַנְטוֹנִינוּס
sources.says: Radak says the sages read the written form as גאים, "proud ones", meaning Rabbi and Antoninus.

25:23.headline: "The older shall serve the younger" can be read either way
25:23.body: The verse has no small word marking who is being served. Radak says it is unclear whether the older serves the younger or the reverse, while Ibn Ezra says the first word is the one doing the action.

sources.quote: לֹא זָכַר עִמָּהֶם מִלַּת ״אֶת״ שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה עַל הַפָּעוּל. וְהִנֵּה הַדָּבָר מְסֻפָּק וְלֹא בֵּאֵר מִי יַעֲבֹד אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, הָרַב אֶת הַצָּעִיר אוֹ הַצָּעִיר אֶת הָרַב
sources.says: Radak says the verse leaves out the marker for the object, so it is unclear whether the older serves the younger or the younger the older.

sources.quote: ורב. הוא הפועל וכן "בן יכבד אב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the older (רב) is the doer, as in "a son honors a father".

25:24.headline: "Twins" is spelled short here, because one twin is wicked
25:24.body: Rashi says תומם is written without an aleph, while Tamar's twins are תאומים with one. Both of hers were righteous, but here one twin was righteous and one was not.

sources.quote: חָסֵר, וּבְתָמָר תְּאוֹמִים מָלֵא, לְפִי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם צַדִּיקִים; אֲבָל כָּאן אֶחָד צַדִּיק וְאֶחָד רָשָׁע
sources.says: Rashi says the word is short here but full for Tamar, because both of hers were righteous and here one is righteous and one wicked.

sources.quote: חָסֵר אָלֶף הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא עֵי״ן הַפֹּעַל, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָשׁ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאֶחָד צַדִּיק וְהָאֶחָד רָשָׁע
sources.says: Radak says the aleph is missing and there is a teaching in it, because one is righteous and one wicked.

25:25.headline: Esau's red color hints that he will spill blood
25:25.body: Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says the red color was a sign Esau would shed blood (דמים). Radak notes that many babies are born red, so אדמוני must mean very red.

sources.quote: סִימָן הוּא שֶׁיְּהֵא שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים
sources.says: Rashi says the red color is a sign he will be a shedder of blood.

sources.quote: וּבְרֹב הַנּוֹלָדִים יָצְאוּ אֲדֻמִּים, אֶלָּא רַצָּה לוֹמַר אַדְמוֹנִי חָזָק בְּאַדְמִימוּת
sources.says: Radak says most babies come out red, so this word means strongly red.

25:25.headline: Esau's name means "made", as if he was born fully formed
25:25.body: Rashi says everyone called him Esau because he seemed already made and finished, like a man of many years, with all his hair. Rashbam says the same: a man made and complete, with hair.

sources.quote: הַכֹּל קָרְאוּ לוֹ כֵן, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִגְמָר בִּשְׂעָרוֹ כְבֶן שָׁנִים הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says everyone called him this because he was already made and finished, with his hair, like a man of many years.

sources.quote: אדם עשוי ונגמר שהיה בעל שער
sources.says: Rashbam says the name means a man made and complete, who had hair.

25:26.headline: Jacob's name comes from the heel his hand was holding
25:26.body: The verse says his hand held Esau's heel (עקב), and then he was named יעקב. Rashi says his father named him for the grip, and Radak says the grip was also a sign that Jacob would come out on top in the end.

sources.quote: אָבִיו קָרָא לוֹ יַעֲקֹב עַל שֵׁם אֲחִיזַת הֶעָקֵב
sources.says: Rashi says one view is that his father named him Jacob for the holding of the heel.

sources.quote: זֶה הָיָה גַם כֵּן סִימָן כִּי בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה יִשְׁלֹט בְּעֵשָׂו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָדָם שׁוֹלֵט בְּדָבָר שֶׁאוֹחֵז בְּיָדוֹ; וְעָקֵב הוּא סוֹף הַגּוּף
sources.says: Radak says the grip was a sign that Jacob would rule over Esau in the end, since the heel is the end of the body.

25:27.headline: Why "tents" is plural: Jacob sat in more than one
25:27.body: Rashi names the tent of Shem and the tent of Ever, which Bereshit Rabbah calls their houses of study. Sforno says one was a shepherd's tent and the other a tent where he learned about his Creator.

sources.quote: אָהֳלוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם וְאָהֳלוֹ שֶׁל עֵבֶר
sources.says: Rashi says the tents were the tent of Shem and the tent of Ever.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי אֹהָלִים, בֵּית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם וּבֵית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵבֶר
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says the two tents were the house of study of Shem and the house of study of Ever.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי מִינֵי אֹהָלִים: הָאֶחָד אֹהֶל רוֹעִים, וְהַשֵּׁנִי אֹהֶל בַּל יִצְעָן (ישעיהו לג:כ), שֶׁבּוֹ הִתְבּוֹנֵן לְהַכִּיר בּוֹרְאו
sources.says: Sforno says there were two kinds of tent: a shepherd's tent and a tent where he came to know his Creator.

25:28.headline: "Game in his mouth": Isaac's mouth, or Esau's mouth?
25:28.body: Rashi follows the Aramaic translation: Isaac liked the meat in his own mouth. But the midrash says it was Esau's mouth: he trapped his father with his words.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ בְּפִיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ בְּפִיו שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, שֶׁהָיָה צָד אוֹתוֹ וּמְרַמֵּהוּ בִדְבָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads it as in Isaac's mouth, but the midrash reads it as Esau's mouth, with which he trapped and tricked his father.

sources.quote: אָמְרוּ הַמְּפָרְשִׁים (הראב"ע והרד"ק) כִּי יִתֵּן צַיִד בְּפִיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק אוֹ יָבִיא
sources.says: Ramban reports that Ibn Ezra and Radak read it as Esau putting or bringing game into Isaac's mouth.

25:29.headline: "Tired": worn out from murder, or just faint with hunger
25:29.body: Rashi, from Bereshit Rabbah, says Esau was "tired" from killing, as in Jeremiah 4:31. Ibn Ezra says it means faint from hunger and thirst.

sources.quote: בִּרְצִיחָה, כְּמָה דְּתֵימָא כִּי עָיְפָה נַפְשִׁי לְהֹרְגִים
sources.says: Rashi says Esau was tired from murder, as in "my soul is faint before murderers".

sources.quote: כטעם "בארץ עיפה" (ישעי, לב ב) רעב וצמא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means hunger and thirst, as in "a weary land".

25:30.headline: The nickname Edom, "red", mocks Esau for selling his birthright
25:30.body: The verse says Esau was called אדום, "red", because of the red stew. Rashbam says the name was given in scorn, and Sforno reads it as an order: "turn red".

sources.quote: הוא אדמוני ונתאווה לאכול אדום. ובשביל רעבתנותו מכר בכורתו ולשם בזיון קרא לו כן
sources.says: Rashbam says Esau was reddish and craved red food, and the name was given in scorn.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי, כְּלוֹמַר הִתְאַדֵּם וֶהְיֵה צָבוּעַ אָדוֹם בְּהַלְעָטַת הָאָדוֹם
sources.says: Sforno says the word is a command: "turn red" by gulping the red stew.

25:31.headline: "As today": "clearly" to Rashi, "right now" to Rashbam
25:31.body: Jacob tells Esau to sell the birthright כיום. Rashi says it means "as clear as day", a clear and firm sale, while Rashbam says it means "at once".

sources.quote: כַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוּא בָרוּר, כָךְ מְכֹר לִי מְכִירָה בְרוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means "as the day is clear", so Esau must make a clear sale.

sources.quote: לאלתר, מיד מכור לי
sources.says: Rashbam says it means "right away, sell me now".

27:3.headline: "Lift your weapons" also means "sharpen your weapons"
27:3.body: Rashi says שא נא means "sharpen". Isaac is telling Esau to sharpen his knife and slaughter properly, so he does not feed him an animal that died unslaughtered.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן הַשְׁחָזָה, כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין, אֲבָל מַשִּׂיאָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֶרְתָּהּ (ביצה כ"ח), חַדֵּד סַכִּינְךָ וּשְׁחֹט יָפֶה, שֶׁלֹּא תַאֲכִילֵנִי נְבֵלָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means sharpening, so Esau should sharpen his knife and slaughter well and not feed Isaac an unslaughtered carcass.

27:3.headline: תליך is used once, and is either a sword or a quiver
27:3.body: Rashi says it is a sword, since a sword is hung from the belt, and Radak says the Aramaic translation reads it that way too. Rashbam says it is the quiver that hangs with the arrows.

sources.quote: חַרְבְּךָ שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ לִתְלוֹתָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is your sword, which people hang on themselves.

sources.quote: אשפתו שתלויים בה החצים
sources.says: Rashbam says it is his quiver, in which the arrows hang.

sources.quote: וְאֻנְקְלוֹס תִּרְגֵּם ״סַיְפָך
sources.says: Radak says Onkelos translated it as "your sword".

27:3.headline: An extra ה in "game" hints at the five laws of slaughter
27:3.body: The verse is written צידה but read צָיִד, "game". Radak says the sages explained the extra ה as a hint to five laws of slaughter.

sources.quote: נִכְתַּב הַהֵ״א לִרְמֹז בָּהּ חָמֵשׁ הֲלָכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה
sources.says: Radak says the written ה hints at the five rules of slaughter, in the known teaching.

27:7.headline: Rebecca adds "before God" to what Isaac asked
27:7.body: Isaac asked only that he might bless Esau, but Rebecca adds "before God". Rashi says it means with God's approval, and Ramban says she meant the blessing would be given by the holy spirit.

sources.quote: בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, שֶׁיַּסְכִּים עַל יָדִי
sources.says: Rashi says "before God" means with His permission, so that He agrees with me.

sources.quote: לֹא נִזְכַּר בְּכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה לִפְנֵי ה' רַק בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה, כִּי אָמְרָה לוֹ אִמּוֹ הַבְּרָכָה לִפְנֵי ה' תִּהְיֶה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶש
sources.says: Ramban says "before God" appears nowhere else in this account, because Rebecca told Jacob the blessing would be given by the holy spirit.

27:19.headline: "I am Esau your firstborn" can be split into two true statements
27:19.body: Rashi reads it as "I am the one bringing you food, and Esau is your firstborn." Ibn Ezra mentions others who said Jacob spoke softly on אנכי and raised his voice on "Esau your firstborn".

sources.quote: אָנֹכִי הַמֵּבִיא לְךָ וְעֵשָׂו הוּא בְּכוֹרֶך
sources.says: Rashi reads it as "I am the one bringing you food, and Esau is your firstborn".

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו כי בנחת אמר אנכי, ונשא קול במלת עשו בכורך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says others held that Jacob said "I am" quietly and raised his voice at "Esau your firstborn".

27:22.headline: The "voice of Jacob" is his polite speech, and also his strength
27:22.body: Rashi says Isaac noticed Jacob's pleading words ("please get up"), where Esau would speak harshly. Bereshit Rabbah says Jacob's power is in his voice, and Esau's is in his hands.

sources.quote: שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּחֲנוּנִים קוּם נָא, אֲבָל עֵשָׂו קִנְטוּרְיָא דִּבֵּר יָקֻם אָבִי
sources.says: Rashi says the voice is Jacob's because he spoke in pleading language, "please get up", while Esau would say "let my father rise" harshly.

sources.quote: אֵין יַעֲקֹב שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא בְּקוֹלוֹ, הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו, אֵין עֵשָׂו שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא בַּיָּדָיִם
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Jacob rules only with his voice, and Esau rules only with his hands.

27:27.headline: "See the smell of my son": seeing stands in for smelling
27:27.body: Isaac says רְאֵה, "see", about a smell, and Maimonides says Hebrew often uses one sense for another, with this verse as an example. Ibn Ezra says ראה here means speaking to the heart.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 46:5
sources.quote: וכן "רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי [כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה']" (בראשית כז,כז), כאילו אמר "אריח ריח בני", כי המכוון הוא השגת ריחו
sources.says: Maimonides says "see the smell of my son" is as if he said "smell", because one sense is used for another.

sources.quote: ראה. דבור עם הלב, והיה ריח טוב בבגדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ראה here is speaking to the heart, and that the clothes had a good smell.

27:28.headline: "The God" in the blessing means God as judge
27:28.body: Rashi asks why the verse says הָאֱלֹהִים, "the Elohim", and answers: God as judge, who gives only if Jacob deserves it. Maimonides notes that אלהים is also the word for judges.

sources.quote: מַהוּ הָאֱלֹהִים? בַּדִּין; אִם רָאוּי לְךָ יִתֵּן לְךָ וְאִם לָאו לֹא יִתֵּן לְך
sources.says: Rashi says "the Elohim" means in judgment: if it is fitting for you He will give, and if not He will not.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 2, Chapter 6:1
sources.quote: ידוע לך כבר ש"אלהים" הוא שם השופטים
sources.says: Maimonides says אלהים is the name for judges.

27:29.headline: "Sons of your mother", because Isaac had only one wife
27:29.body: Rashi says Jacob later told Judah "sons of your father" because he had children by several wives, while Isaac had only one wife, so he says "sons of your mother". Rashbam says the same.

sources.quote: וְיַעֲקֹב אָמַר לִיהוּדָה בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ, לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָנִים מִכַּמָּה אִמָּהוֹת, וְכָאן, שֶׁלֹּא נָשָׂא אֶלָּא אִשָּׁה אַחַת, אוֹמֵר בְּנֵי אִמֶּך
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob said "sons of your father" to Judah because he had several wives, but here, with one wife, it says "sons of your mother".

sources.quote: אבל ביעקב שהיו לו נשים הרבה, כתוב בו: וישתחוו לך בני אביך
sources.says: Rashbam says Jacob had many wives, and so it says "sons of your father" there.

27:33.headline: Isaac "trembled": amazed, or seeing Gehenna open beneath him
27:33.body: Rashi says the Aramaic translation takes it as amazement, and the midrash says Isaac saw Gehenna open beneath him. Radak says he showed great fear so Esau would not think he had helped trick him.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וּתְוַהּ, לְשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ רָאָה גֵּיהִנֹּם פְּתוּחָה מִתַּחְתָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads it as amazement, and the midrash says he saw Gehenna open beneath him.

sources.quote: הֶרְאָה חֲרָדָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּעַצְמוֹ בִּפְנֵי עֵשָׂו, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשֹׁב עָלָיו עֵשָׂו כִּי בְּכַוָּנָה עָשָׂה יִצְחָק מַה שֶּׁבֵּרַךְ אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְהֵתֵל בּו
sources.says: Radak says Isaac showed great fear in front of Esau so Esau would not think he had blessed Jacob on purpose and mocked him.

27:33.headline: "Who then?" or "who, where?": the little word אפוא
27:33.body: Rashi says אפוא is made of איה פה, "where here", so Isaac asks "who is he, and where?" Sforno says that spelled with an aleph it means "if so", so Isaac asks "if so, who was it?"

sources.quote: אֵיפֹה – אַיֵּה פֹה, מִי הוּא וְאֵיפֹה הוּא הַצָּד צַיִד
sources.says: Rashi says "where" is "where here", so it means "who is he and where is he, the one who hunted game".

sources.quote: כִּי אָמְנָם מִלַּת אֵיפוֹא כְּשֶׁתָּבֹא עִם אָלֶ"ף בְּסוֹף הַתֵּיבָה מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בִּמְקוֹם אִם כֵּן
sources.says: Sforno says that with an aleph at the end the word stands for "if so", while with a ה it means "where".

27:35.headline: "Deceit" or "wisdom"? Commentators read מרמה different ways
27:35.body: Isaac says Jacob came בְּמִרְמָה: Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Yochanan read it as "with the wisdom of his Torah". Ibn Ezra reads it as "not telling the truth", and Radak says it means he made his hands hairy.

sources.quote: בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר בָּא בְּחָכְמַת תּוֹרָתו
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Rabbi Yochanan read "he came with deceit" as "he came with the wisdom of his Torah".

sources.quote: שלא דבר אמת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he did not speak truth.

sources.quote: שֶׁעָשָׂה יָדָיו שְׂעִירוֹת
sources.says: Radak says the deceit was that he made his hands hairy.

27:36.headline: "Is that why he is called Jacob?" or "Truly he is"
27:36.body: Rashi says הכי is a question of wonder: is it because he was named Jacob that he has now tripped me up? Ibn Ezra and Radak say it means "truly", as in "he is rightly named Jacob".

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן תֵּמַהּ הוּא, כְּמוֹ הֲכִי אָחִי אַתָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of wonder, like "are you my brother?".

sources.quote: כמו אמת וכן "הכי אחי אתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means "truly", and compares it with "are you indeed my brother".

sources.quote: עַל נָכוֹן קָרָא הַקּוֹרֵא שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב
sources.says: Radak says Esau means "he was rightly named Jacob".

27:36.headline: Esau hears Jacob's name inside the word "he cheated me"
27:36.body: Radak says the name יעקב holds two ideas, "heel" and "deceit", and Esau says both came true. Rashi adds that the Aramaic translation reads ויעקבני as "he lay in wait for me", and some read "he outwitted me".

sources.quote: כִּי יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עִנְיָנִים: מִן עָקֵב וּמִרְמָה, כְּמוֹ ״עָקֹב הַלֵּב״ (ירמיה יז:ט), ״כִּי כָל אָח עָקוֹב יַעְקֹב״ (ירמיה ט:ג), וּשְׁנֵיהֶם הָיוּ בו
sources.says: Radak says the name Jacob has two senses, "heel" and "deceit", and both were in him.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וּכְמַנִי – אֲרָבַנִי; וְאָרַב – וּכְמַן. וְיֵשׁ מְתַרְגְּמִין וְחַכְּמַנִי, נִתְחַכֵּם לִי
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads "he lay in ambush for me", and some translate "he outwitted me".

sources.quote: כמו מרמה וכן "בעקבה" (מ"ב י יט), ויתכן היותו מגזרת "עקוב הלב" (ירמי' יז ט), והעקוב הפך המישור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means deceit, and may come from "the heart is crooked", since crooked is the opposite of straight.

27:37.headline: Isaac calls Jacob "master", so what Esau gains is Jacob's
27:37.body: Rashi says that since Isaac made Jacob a master over Esau, whatever Esau acquires belongs to Jacob, as a slave's gains belong to his master. Ramban says a master need not make others slaves.

sources.quote: אִם תִּקְנֶה נְכָסִים, שֶׁלּוֹ הֵם, שֶׁהֲרֵי גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ, וּמַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּו
sources.says: Rashi says if Esau acquires property it is Jacob's, since Isaac made Jacob a master, and what a slave acquires his master acquires.

sources.quote: אֲבָל יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הַגְּבִיר וְלֹא יִהְיוּ הֵם עֲבָדִים
sources.says: Ramban says it is possible that Jacob would be the master without the brothers being slaves.

27:40.headline: תריד can mean "you rule" or "you grieve"
27:40.body: Rashi says תריד means to be distressed, as in אריד בשיחי, "I moan in my complaint". Ibn Ezra says it is either like תרדה, "you will rule", or the same sense Rashi gives.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צַעַר כְּמוֹ אָרִיד בְּשִׂיחִי
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of distress, like "I will moan in my complaint".

sources.quote: כמו תרדה והם ב' שרשים, וי"א כמו "אריד בשיחי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like תרדה, from a different root, and others say it is like "I moan in my complaint".

27:42.headline: Esau "consoles himself" with the thought of killing Jacob
27:42.body: נחם can mean comfort or a change of heart. Rashi gives several readings, including a change of heart about being a brother and comfort in the killing, and Ibn Ezra says his comfort is that he can kill you.

sources.quote: נִחָם עַל הָאַחְוָה לַחֲשֹׁב מַחֲשָׁבָה אַחֶרֶת לְהִתְנַכֵּר לְךָ וּלְהָרְגְּךָ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה כְּבָר אַתָּה מֵת בְּעֵינָיו וְשָׁתָה עָלֶיךָ כּוֹס שֶׁל תַּנְחוּמִים. וּלְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ לְשׁוֹן תַּנְחוּמִים, מִתְנַחֵם הוּא עַל הַבְּרָכוֹת בַּהֲרִיגָתְך
sources.says: Rashi gives several readings: a change of heart about brotherhood, the cup of consolation for one already dead, or comfort over the blessings by killing him.

sources.quote: זאת היא נחמתו שיוכל להרגך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says his comfort is that he will be able to kill you.

3:1.headline: The serpent’s cunning echoes the humans’ nakedness
3:1.body: Ibn Ezra points out the sound play between ערום, “cunning,” and ערומים, “naked,” in the previous verse. The similar words carry different meanings.

sources.quote: ופי' ערום חכם שיעשה דבריו בערמה, ואל תתמה בעבור היות ערום אחר ערומים, והם שני טעמים, כי באלה הצחות בלשון, כמו "בלחי החמור חמור חמורתים (שופ', טו טז), וכן "על שלשים עיירים, ושלשים עיירים להם" (שם יו"ד ד),
sources.says: Ibn Ezra points out a sound play between ערום and ערומים.

3:3.headline: Eve adds a ban on touching the tree
3:3.body: Rashi notices that תגעו, “touch,” adds a restriction God had not given. He says this addition helped lead to breaking the command.

sources.quote: ולא תגעו בו. הוֹסִיפָה עַל הַצִּוּוּי, לְפִיכָךְ בָּאָה לִידֵי גֵרָעוֹן, הוּא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַל תּוֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָיו (משלי ל'):
sources.says: Rashi says Eve’s added restriction helped lead her to break the command.

3:5.headline: Like rulers, or like creators of worlds
3:5.body: Maimonides follows Onkelos in reading כאלהים as “like rulers.” Rashi reads the serpent’s promise as the power to create worlds.

sources.quote: ולפני שאפרט את הקושיה ופתרונה אקדים שכל דובר עברית יודע שהמונח 'אלהים' משותף א) לאלוה ב) ולמלאכים ג) ולשופטים מנהיגי המדינות. וכבר ביאר אנקלוס הגר עליו השלום, ואמת מה שביאר, שבפסוק "וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים יֹדְעֵי טוֹב וָרָע" (בראשית ג,ה) הכוונה למשמעות האחרונה, ותרגם: "וּתְהוֹן כְּרַבְרְבִין" (=ותהיו כגדולים, כנכבדים).
sources.says: Maimonides says Onkelos understands אלהים here as human judges and rulers.

sources.quote: והייתם כאלהים. יוֹצְרֵי עוֹלָמוֹת (בראשית רבה):
sources.says: Rashi explains the promise as becoming creators of worlds.

3:7.headline: Their eyes open to a new sense of shame
3:7.body: Maimonides says ותפקחנה describes a change in judgment: they now find nakedness shameful. Their eyesight has not changed.

sources.quote: התבונן בנאמר: "וַתִּפָּקַחְנָה עֵינֵי שְׁנֵיהֶם וַיֵּדְעוּ כִּי עֵירֻמִּם הֵם" (בראשית ג,ז). לא נאמר 'ותפקחנה עיני שניהם ויראו', משום שמה שראה לפני כן הוא אשר ראה לאחר מכן. לא היה כיסוי על עיניו שהוסר, אלא נוצר לו מצב אחר, שבו הוא ראה כמגונה מה שלא ראה כמגונה קודם לכן.
sources.says: Maimonides says their sight was unchanged, but nakedness now seemed shameful.

sources.quote: ותפקחנה וגו'. לְעִנְיַן הַחָכְמָה דִּבֵּר הַכָּתוּב וְלֹא לְעִנְיַן רְאִיָּה מַמָּשׁ, וְסוֹף הַמִּקְרָא מוֹכִיחַ:
sources.says: Rashi says the opening concerns understanding rather than physical sight.

3:7.headline: They are also stripped of their one commandment
3:7.body: Rashi asks why nakedness needed to be discovered when even a blind person knows they are naked. He reads עירמם as also meaning that they have lost the one commandment entrusted to them.

sources.quote: וידעו כי עירמים הם. אַף הַסּוּמָא יוֹדֵעַ כְּשֶׁהוּא עָרוּם, אֶלָּא מַהוּ וַיֵּדְעוּ כִּי עֵירֻמִּם הֵם? מִצְוָה אַחַת הָיְתָה בְיָדָם וְנִתְעַרְטְלוּ הֵימֶנָּה (בראשית רבה):
sources.says: Rashi says they had one commandment and were stripped of it.

3:8.headline: The sound is moving through the garden
3:8.body: Maimonides reads מתהלך, “walking,” as describing God’s voice spreading through the garden. The word can describe a sound traveling, without anyone taking steps.

sources.quote: ג) לאחר מכן הושאל להתפשטות דבר כלשהו והופעתו, גם אם אין הוא גשמי כלל. נאמר: "קוֹלָהּ כַּנָּחָשׁ יֵלֵךְ" (ירמיהו מו,כב). וכיוצא בזה דבריו "[וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת] קוֹל ה' אֱלֹהִים מִתְהַלֵּךְ בַּגָּן" (בראשית ג,ח), הקול הוא שנאמר לגביו שהיה מתהלך.
sources.says: Maimonides says the voice is what the verse describes as moving.

3:8.headline: A direction toward sunset, or the evening breeze
3:8.body: Rashi reads רוח as a direction: west, where the sun sets. Ibn Ezra reads it as the breeze near evening.

sources.quote: לרוח היום. לְאוֹתוֹ רוּחַ שֶׁהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בָּאָה לְשָׁם, וְזוֹ הִיא מַעֲרָבִית; שֶׁלִּפְנוֹת עֶרֶב חַמָּה בַּמַּעֲרָב, וְהֵם סָרְחוּ בָּעֲשִׂירִית (סנהדרין ל"ח):
sources.says: Rashi reads the phrase as the western direction at the approach of evening.

sources.quote: וישמעו מתהלך בגן., קול השם, וזה היה סמוך לערב בעת התנופף רוח היום,
sources.says: Ibn Ezra places the event near evening when the day’s breeze is blowing.

sources.quote: 2 ב) הוא גם שם הרוח המנשבת: "וְרוּחַ הַקָּדִים נָשָׂא אֶת הָאַרְבֶּה" (שמות י,יג), "רוּחַ יָם" (שם,יט). וזה נפוץ.
sources.says: Maimonides lists a blowing wind as one meaning of רוח.

3:15.headline: Crushing and hissing share the sound of the punishment
3:15.body: Rashi reads ישופך as crushing the serpent’s head, but links תשופנו to the hiss before its bite. He says the verse uses matching sounds for the two attacks.

sources.quote: ישופך. יְכַתֶּתְךָ (סוטה ט') כְּמוֹ וָאֶכֹּת אֹתוֹ (דברים ט), וְתַרְגּוּמוֹ וְשָׁפִית יָתֵי':
sources.says: Rashi explains ישופך as crushing.

sources.quote: ואתה תשופנו עקב. לֹא יְהֵא לְךָ קוֹמָה וְתִשְּׁכֶנּוּ בַּעֲקֵבוֹ, וְאַף מִשָּׁם תְּמִיתֶנּוּ, וּלְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ כְּמוֹ נָשַׁף בָּהֶם (ישעיהו מ') כְּשֶׁהַנָּחָשׁ בָּא לִנְשֹׁך הוּא נוֹשֵׁף כְּמִין שְׁרִיקָה וּלְפִי שֶׁהַלָּשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל הַלָּשָוֹן כְּתִיב לְשׁוֹן נְשִׁיפָה בִשְׁנֵיהֶם:
sources.says: Rashi links תשופנו to a serpent’s hissing and explicitly identifies a play between the two expressions.

3:16.headline: Desire and obedience give two different readings
3:16.body: Ibn Ezra reads תשוקתך as obedience to the husband. Ramban rejects that meaning and reads a longing for him despite the pain of pregnancy and childbirth.

sources.quote: תשוקתך. משמעתך, והטעם שתשמעי כל אשר יצוה עליך כי את ברשותו לעשות חפצו:
sources.says: Ibn Ezra explains תשוקתך as obeying the husband’s commands.

sources.quote: וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּקָה רַק בְּחֵשֶׁק וְתַאֲוָה. וְהַנָּכוֹן בְּעֵינַי שֶׁהֶעֱנִישׁ אוֹתָהּ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה נִכְסֶפֶת מְאֹד אֶל בַּעְלָהּ, וְלֹא תָּחוּשׁ לְצַעַר הַהֵרָיוֹן וְהַלֵּדָה,
sources.says: Ramban says תשוקה means desire and reads the verse as longing for the husband despite pregnancy and childbirth.

3:22.headline: The tree may promise a long life rather than immortality
3:22.body: Ibn Ezra says the tree of life would add many years to a person’s life. He reads לעולם here as a long duration, not endless life.

sources.quote: ועץ החיים. שיוסיף חיים ויחיה האדם שנים רבות ואין מלת לעולם עד עולם ועד, והנה כן "ועבדו לעולם" (שמות כא ו) "וישב שם עד עולם" (ש"א א כב), ורבים אחרים,
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the tree extends life for many years and that לעולם need not mean forever.

32:4.headline: Were Jacob's "messengers" real angels? Rashi says yes
32:4.body: מלאכים means both angels and human messengers. Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says these were real angels, while Ibn Ezra says they were Jacob's servants, and Maimonides cites this verse as an example of a human messenger.

sources.quote: מַלְאָכִים מַמָּש
sources.says: Rashi says these were real angels.

sources.quote: ואלה המלאכים הם מעבדיו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these messengers were some of his servants.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 2, Chapter 6:2
sources.quote: מלאך" נאמר א) על שליח מבני האדם: "וַיִּשְׁלַח יַעֲקֹב מַלְאָכִים
sources.says: Maimonides says מלאך is said of a human messenger, and gives "Jacob sent messengers" as the example.

32:5.headline: גרתי adds up to 613, the number of commandments
32:5.body: Rashi says Jacob's "I lived with Laban" (גרתי) has the letter-value 613. He is telling Esau that he kept all the commandments while living with Laban.

sources.quote: גַּרְתִּי בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא תרי"ג, כְּלוֹמַר, עִם לָבָן גַּרְתִּי וְתַרְיַ"ג מִצְוֹת שָׁמַרְתִּי וְלֹא לָמַדְתִּי מִמַּעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים
sources.says: Rashi says גרתי adds up to 613, meaning Jacob lived with Laban and kept the 613 commandments and did not learn from his wicked deeds.

32:8.headline: Two kinds of fear: of being killed, and of having to kill
32:8.body: The verse says Jacob "feared" and "was distressed". Rashi says the first is fear of being killed and the second is distress at the thought of killing others.

sources.quote: וַיִּירָא שֶׁמָּא יֵהָרֵג, וַיֵּצֶר לוֹ אִם יַהֲרֹג הוּא אֶת אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says "he feared" that he might be killed, and "he was distressed" at the thought that he himself might kill others.

32:13.headline: Jacob's "surely good" splits into his merit and his fathers'
32:13.body: God said "I will surely do good with you". Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, reads the doubled verb as two promises: one for Jacob's own merit, one for his fathers' merit.

sources.quote: הֵיטֵב בִּזְכוּתְךָ, אֵיטִיב בִּזְכוּת אֲבוֹתֶיך
sources.says: Rashi says "do good" is for your merit and "I will do good" is for your fathers' merit.

32:17.headline: "Space" between the herds was meant to astonish Esau
32:17.body: Jacob tells his servants to leave a gap (רוח) between the herds. Rashi says it let Esau's eye take in each herd and marvel at the size of the gift, while Ibn Ezra says the word means a pause, as with relief between blows.

sources.quote: עֵדֶר לִפְנֵי חֲבֵרוֹ מְלֹא עַיִן, כְּדֵי לְהַשְׂבִּיעַ עֵינוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע וּלְתַוֵּהוּ עַל רִבּוּי הַדּוֹרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says each herd should be an eyeful before the next, to satisfy the wicked one's eye and amaze him at the size of the gift.

sources.quote: הפרש, וקרוב ממנו "כי היתה הרוחה" (שמות ח יא), הפרשה בין מכה למכה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means a gap, close to "there was relief", the break between one plague and the next.

32:21.headline: "Face" also means anger, as in "wipe away his face"
32:21.body: Ibn Ezra says פניו here means his anger. Maimonides lists "anger" among the meanings of פנים, and cites "her face was no longer hers".

sources.quote: ופניו כעסו וכן "ופניה לא הי' לה עוד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says his face means his anger, as in "her face was no longer hers".

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 37:2
sources.quote: הוא שמו של הכעס: "וּפָנֶיהָ לֹא הָיוּ לָהּ עוֹד
sources.says: Maimonides says פנים is also the name of anger, and cites "her face was no longer hers".

32:25.headline: "Left alone" means Jacob went back for small jars
32:25.body: Rashi says the word "left" hints that Jacob had forgotten small jars and went back for them. Rashbam gives a plain reading: Jacob stayed behind alone, meaning to slip away by another road.

sources.quote: שָׁכַח פַּכִּים קְטַנִּים וְחָזַר עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says he forgot small jars and went back for them.

sources.quote: ורצה לעבור אחריהם, כדי לברוח דרך אחרת שלא יפגשנו עשו
sources.says: Rashbam says Jacob wanted to cross after them and flee by another way so Esau would not meet him.

32:25.headline: "Wrestled" may come from dust, or from a hug and a tie
32:25.body: Ibn Ezra and Radak link ויאבק to אבק, "dust", raised by their feet. Rashi says it is an Aramaic word for binding, as wrestlers grip and embrace each other.

sources.quote: וְלִי נִרְאֶה שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁר, וְלָשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי הוּא, בָּתַר דַּאֲבִיקוּ בֵיהּ, וַאֲבֵיק לֵיהּ מֵיבַק – לְשׁוֹן עֲנִיבָה, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ שְׁנַיִם שֶׁמִּתְעַצְּמִים לְהַפִּיל אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ, שֶׁחוֹבְקוֹ וְאוֹבְקוֹ בִּזְרוֹעוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is an Aramaic word meaning "tie", since wrestlers hug and grip each other in their arms.

sources.quote: מגזרת אבק, עד שעלה אבק ביניהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from "dust", until dust rose between them.

sources.quote: נִתְאַבֵּק עִמּוֹ עַד שֶׁהֶעֱלוּ אָבָק
sources.says: Radak says he wrestled with him until they raised dust.

32:25.headline: The "man" who wrestled Jacob is an angel, say the commentators
32:25.body: איש means "man", but Radak says here it is an angel who looks like a man, and Maimonides says the whole scene was a vision. Rashi adds that the sages said he was Esau's guardian angel.

sources.quote: מַלְאָךְ, וְכֵן ״וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ עֹמֵד לְנֶגְדּו
sources.says: Radak says איש here means an angel, as in "behold, a man standing opposite him".

sources.quote: וּפֵרְשׁוּ רַזִ"לִ שֶׁהוּא שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explained that he was Esau's guardian angel.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 2, Chapter 42:3
sources.quote: וכן אני אומר גם בפרשת יעקב על דבריו "וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ" (בראשית לב,כה), שזה בצורת התגלות, כיוון שהתברר לבסוף שהוא מלאך
sources.says: Maimonides says the wrestling was a revealed vision, since it became clear in the end that he was an angel.

32:26.headline: "Pulled loose": a word that can also mean "pitch a tent"
32:26.body: Rashi says the hip socket was pulled out of its joint, and compares "lest my soul be torn from you". Chizkuni says some words flip between building and tearing down, and gives this one: it can mean to tear out, or to pitch a tent.

sources.quote: נִתְקַעְקְעָה מִמְּקוֹם מַחְבַּרְתָּהּ, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ פֶּן תֵּקַע נַפְשִׁי מִמֵּךְ (ירמיהו ו'), לְשׁוֹן הֲסָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it was pulled out from its joint, like "lest my soul be torn from you", a word of removal.

sources.quote: יש דברים ובפתרונם מתהפכים לשתי מליצות בנין וסתירה כגון זה. וכגון פן תקע נפשי ממך ומצינו ויעקב תקע את אהלו בהר
sources.says: Chizkuni says some words can mean both building and destroying, and gives this word, comparing "pitch his tent on the mountain".

32:29.headline: The name Israel is explained as "you strove" or "you became great"
32:29.body: The verse explains the name with כי שרית. Onkelos translates it as "you became great before the Lord", Rashbam derives it from "in his strength he strove with God", and Chizkuni says Jacob became equal to angels in authority but not over them.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי רַבְרְבַת קֳדָם יְי
sources.says: Onkelos says "for you have become great before the Lord".

sources.quote: מגזרת באונו שרה את אלהים כמו קנה קנית. עשה עשית
sources.says: Rashbam says שרית comes from "in his strength he strove with God", a past form like קנה קנית.

sources.quote: נעשית שווה למלאכים בשררה וממשלה אבל לא עליהם
sources.says: Chizkuni says Jacob became equal to angels in authority and rule, but not over them.

32:30.headline: The angel will not give his name: it changes with each mission
32:30.body: Jacob asks the angel's name. Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says angels have no fixed name because it changes with each mission, and Ramban says knowing it would not help Jacob, since all power belongs to God alone.

sources.quote: אֵין לָנוּ שֵׁם קָבוּעַ, מִשְׁתַּנִּים שְׁמוֹתֵנוּ, הַכֹּל לְפִי מִצְוַת עֲבוֹדַת הַשְּׁלִיחוּת שֶׁאָנוּ מִשְׁתַּלְּחִים
sources.says: Rashi says angels have no fixed name; their names change according to the mission they are sent on.

sources.quote: אֵין לְךָ בִּידִיעַת שְׁמִי תּוֹעֶלֶת, כִּי אֵין הַכֹּחַ וְהַיְּכֹלֶת בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּו
sources.says: Ramban says knowing the angel's name would not help Jacob, since power belongs only to God.

32:33.headline: The "thigh sinew" is named for jumping out of place
32:33.body: Rashi says the sinew is called הנשה because it leaped (נשה) from its place and went up. Radak says the same: it was torn loose and rose onto the socket.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁנָּשָׁה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ וְעָלָה, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן קְפִיצָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is named this because it leaped from its place and went up, a word of jumping.

sources.quote: נִקְרָא כֵּן לְפִי שֶׁנָּשָׁה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ וְעָלָה (חולין צא), כְּלוֹמַר נִפְסַק וְנֶעֱלָה עַל הַכַּף שֶׁהוּא דָּבֵק בּו
sources.says: Radak says it is called this because it moved from its place and rose, torn loose and lifted onto the socket it clung to.
